query: What is movable property under BNS?

phase8.query: What is movable property under BNS?

variants.name: original
variants.query: What is movable property under BNS?

original.text: “movable property” includes property of every description, except land and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything which is attached to the earth;
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 1: PRELIMINARY
Section 2: Definitions.
“movable property” includes property of every description, except land and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything which is attached to the earth;

original.text: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person’s consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 303: Theft.
Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person’s consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.

original.text: A moving effected by the same act which affects the severance may be a theft.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 303: Theft.
Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person’s consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
A moving effected by the same act which affects the severance may be a theft.

original.text: The consent mentioned in this section may be express or implied, and may be given either by the person in possession, or by any person having for that purpose authority either express or implied.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 303: Theft.
Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person’s consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
The consent mentioned in this section may be express or implied, and may be given either by the person in possession, or by any person having for that purpose authority either express or implied.

original.text: A person is said to cause a thing to move by removing an obstacle which prevented it from moving or by separating it from any other thing, as well as by actually moving it.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 303: Theft.
Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person’s consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
A person is said to cause a thing to move by removing an obstacle which prevented it from moving or by separating it from any other thing, as well as by actually moving it.

original.text: A thing so long as it is attached to the earth, not being movable property, is not the subject of theft; but it becomes capable of being the subject of theft as soon as it is severed from the earth.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 303: Theft.
Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person’s consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
A thing so long as it is attached to the earth, not being movable property, is not the subject of theft; but it becomes capable of being the subject of theft as soon as it is severed from the earth.

original.text: If A owes money to Z for repairing the watch, and if Z retains the watch lawfully as a security for the debt, and A takes the watch out of Z’s possession, with the intention of depriving Z of the property as a security for his debt, he commits theft, in as much as he takes it dishonestly.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 303: Theft.
Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person’s consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
If A owes money to Z for repairing the watch, and if Z retains the watch lawfully as a security for the debt, and A takes the watch out of Z’s possession, with the intention of depriving Z of the property as a security for his debt, he commits theft, in as much as he takes it dishonestly.

original.text: A finds a ring belonging to Z on a table in the house which Z occupies. Here the ring is in Z’s possession, and if A dishonestly removes it, A commits theft.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 303: Theft.

original.text: A takes an article belonging to Z out of Z’s possession without Z’s consent, with the intention of keeping it until he obtains money from Z as a reward for its restoration. Here A takes dishonestly; A has therefore committed theft.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 303: Theft.
Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person’s consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.

original.text: Theft is snatching if, in order to commit theft, the offender suddenly or quickly or forcibly seizes or secures or grabs or takes away from any person or from his possession any movable property.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 304: Snatching.
Theft is snatching if, in order to commit theft, the offender suddenly or quickly or forcibly seizes or secures or grabs or takes away from any person or from his possession any movable property.
